ai.description: *Boiga nuchalis* is a slender, medium-sized snake reaching 1.5m. It is brown with dark, irregular crossbands and a distinctive pale, black-bordered collar on the nape. It features a prominent, blunt head.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga nuchalis* is best distinguished by the prominent, broad black collar on its nape, which is bordered by a distinct white or yellow band, unlike other Indian cat snakes.
ai.habitat: *Boiga nuchalis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations ranging from near sea level up to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Collared Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal, often prowling through tree branches and forest edges under the cover of darkness to hunt for lizards and small birds.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga nuchalis* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga nuchalis* is found in the Western Ghats of India, spanning states like Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, typically at elevations from sea level to 1,200 meters.
